stem: Meera waters the money plant on her balcony every morning. Her teacher asks her to observe the leaf surface under a microscope. She notices many tiny pores on the leaf surface. What is the role of these tiny pores (stomata)?

options.text: They allow the exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen during photosynthesis.
They transport water from the roots to all parts of the plant.
They absorb sunlight so that the leaf can make food.
They hold the leaf firmly to the stem during strong winds.

teacher.key_rationale: Stomata are tiny pores on leaf surfaces that act as the pathway for exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen during photosynthesis, so A is correct. Water transport is the role of xylem (B), sunlight absorption is the role of chlorophyll in chloroplasts (C), and stomata have no structural support role (D).
